commit.message:
[Service Workers] A fetch restarted after a service-worker-generated redirect can lose its ServiceWorkerGlobalScope entry
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=307597

Reviewed by Youenn Fablet.

When a service worker answers a subresource fetch with a redirect and the
request follows it, the network process restarts the fetch through the
service worker with the same fetch identifier. The previous fetch's removal
from ServiceWorkerGlobalScope travelled from the worker thread to the main
thread and back, while the new StartFetch reaches the worker thread directly
from the IPC queue. When the new fetch arrived first, addFetchTask() hit
ASSERT(!m_ongoingFetchTasks.contains(key)), and the late removeFetchTask()
then dropped the new fetch's entry, so a later cancelFetch() for it was
ignored.

Make SWContextManager::removeFetch() callable from any thread, using the
lock-protected worker map, and call it directly from
WebServiceWorkerFetchTaskClient::cleanup(). On redirection, clean up before
sending the redirect response, so the removal is queued on the worker run
loop before the network process can restart the fetch. Navigation fetch
bookkeeping still goes through the main thread; navigation redirects create
a new fetch with a new identifier.

The assertion is only reached when the service worker runs in its own
process, as it did on the GTK and WPE bots, which run Release with
assertions. This ungardens redirected-response.https.html.

* LayoutTests/platform/glib/TestExpectations:
* Source/WebCore/workers/service/context/SWContextManager.cpp:
(WebCore::SWContextManager::removeFetch):
* Source/WebCore/workers/service/context/SWContextManager.h:
* Source/WebKit/WebProcess/Storage/WebServiceWorkerFetchTaskClient.cpp:
(WebKit::WebServiceWorkerFetchTaskClient::didReceiveRedirection):
(WebKit::WebServiceWorkerFetchTaskClient::cleanup):
